newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Tel "satisfied" with H1 performance.
newsitem.headline: HK Tel "satisfied" with H1 performance.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd chief executive Linus Cheung on Tuesday said he was satisfied with the company's 12.1 percent rise in interim net profit.
"A double digit growth rate in such a severly competitive market is no mean feat and we are satisfied," Cheung told a news conference.
He said the company began three years ago to position the the company to meet increasingly aggressive competition.
"I am encouraged today by the result of this effort, and am confident that we are delivering on our plan to maintain growth," he said.
Cheung noted the company had successfully cut costs and boosted revenues, adding he hoped the increase in revenues would be better in the fiscal year's second half than in the first.
Overall operating costs grew eight percent for the six months to September 30, versus revenue growth of 9.3 percent and compared to seven percent growth in the previous period.
The operating margin improved to 38 percent from 37 percent in the previous period.
Cheung said the company's plan to reduce its workforce by 2,500 over three years was well on target, with staff cut by 1,000 in the first half to 14,000.
Mobile services provided strong revenue growth in the first half with the number of customers rising to 320,000 with capacity for 600,000, he said.
Hongkong Telecom is about 58 percent owned by Cable and Wireless Plc.
